audit_findings.title: FY2025 earnings predate a material July 2026 funding shock
audit_findings.magnitude: 36,334 graduate and doctoral students, computed as 42.6% of 85,306 fall-2025 USHE students; post-July-2026 financial impact unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Reduced financing can lower enrollment, revenue, OE and achievable growth below the $123.5 million historical anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: OBBBA eliminates, effective July 2026, Federal Direct PLUS loans for graduate and professional students, with some limited grandfathering for current graduate and professional student borrowers.
audit_findings.explanation: The financing change is demonstrated and was effective by the valuation date, but no post-July enrollment or earnings effect is in the record. The exposed student population is large enough to warrant close monitoring, while actual use of Grad PLUS, grandfathering and replacement funding remain unknown.
audit_findings.action: Obtain post-July-2026 starts, enrollment, persistence, financing gaps and revenue by affected graduate program; then rerun the anchor and growth cases, including a negative-growth case, if deterioration is observed.

audit_findings.title: Borrower-defense recoupment is an unquantified claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: 8,640 applications in the cited 2024-notice set, plus 4,251 additional claims scheduled for May-July 2026; cash exposure unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Successful recoupment would create a cash claim senior to common equity, reducing the cash bridge or future OE if paid from operations.
audit_findings.evidence: Since the Department’s 2024 notices, Capella University has received approximately 6,770 applications, and Strayer University has received approximately 1,870 applications.
audit_findings.explanation: The large claim population is demonstrated, but no adjudication, recoupment demand, principal amount, probability-weighted loss or booked reserve is supplied. The record therefore cannot establish whether the exposure is material relative to the $128.752 million cash add-on or the $123.5 million OE anchor.
audit_findings.action: Obtain claim-level loan principal, approval and discharge outcomes, applicable BDTR rules, recoupment notices, defenses, insurance and legal probability assessments; calculate expected and adverse-case cash exposure and rerun the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Regulatory collateral could make added cash unavailable to shareholders
audit_findings.magnitude: 10% to 50% of institution-level prior-year Title IV funds per triggering event, with stacking permitted; dollar exposure unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Letters of credit or cash escrow would encumber bridge cash and could add financing costs that reduce OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The amount of financial protection can range from 10% up to 50% of Title IV funds per triggering event, and the Department may “stack” financial protection requirements if more than one mandatory or discretionary trigger is present.
audit_findings.explanation: The collateral framework is demonstrated, but the record identifies no imposed protection requirement or confirmed triggering event and does not provide institution-level Title IV receipts needed to calculate dollars. Materiality to the $128.752 million cash bridge therefore remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Confirm all reported or pending triggers with the Department, obtain prior-year Title IV receipts separately for Capella and Strayer, calculate single and stacked collateral requirements, and rerun the bridge after excluding encumbered cash and adding financing costs.

audit_findings.title: Strayer was only 0.36 percentage point below the 90/10 ceiling
audit_findings.magnitude: 89.64% in 2024, leaving 0.36 percentage point of headroom; 87.98% in audited 2025, leaving 2.02 percentage points
audit_findings.mechanism: A breach could cause provisional certification, and consecutive breaches could remove Title IV eligibility, sharply reducing enrollment and OE.
audit_findings.evidence: For fiscal year 2024, Strayer University derived approximately 89.64% of its cash-basis revenues from federal education assistance.
audit_findings.explanation: The narrow 2024 margin is demonstrated, but the subsequently filed 2025 ratio improved by 1.66 percentage points and remained compliant. There is no present breach in the numbers; the discontinuous downside remains a forward-looking risk because the 2026 ratio is unavailable.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the current 2026 calculation and its federal and non-federal revenue components; monitor monthly headroom and rerun enrollment and OE only if the ratio approaches or exceeds 90%.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized cloud spending may sit outside the OE reinvestment deduction
audit_findings.magnitude: Cloud-computing assets increased from $27.730 million at December 31, 2024 to $36.015 million at December 31, 2025, a computed $8.285 million increase equal to 6.7% of the $123.5 million OE anchor; cash additions remain unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Capitalized implementation cash outlays reduce owner earnings but may be omitted if OE deducts only PP&E capital expenditures; amortization timing can defer recognition of the economic reinvestment.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company defers implementation costs incurred in cloud computing arrangements and amortizes these costs over the term of the arrangement.
audit_findings.explanation: The capitalized asset growth is demonstrated and is large enough relative to anchor OE to affect value. The supplied record does not include the OE worksheet or gross cash additions, so the omission itself is unresolved, but its demonstrated scale makes it reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile OE line by line to operating and investing cash flows; obtain gross cloud-implementation additions, related amortization and deferred contract-cost additions, then rerun OE after deducting recurring cash reinvestment not already captured.

audit_findings.title: Not all cash may be distributable at face value
audit_findings.magnitude: $128.752 million bridge addition, comprising $123.755 million cash and equivalents plus $4.997 million current marketable securities; unavailable portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Foreign taxes or restrictions and minimum regulatory or operating liquidity would reduce the excess cash added in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company intends to indefinitely reinvest its foreign earnings and cash unless such repatriation results in no or minimal tax costs.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates an indefinite-reinvestment policy, but it does not allocate bridge cash by entity or jurisdiction or quantify minimum operating liquidity. The separately reported $7.891 million of restricted cash is held in other current assets and is not part of the stated bridge addition, so that known restricted balance is already excluded; any further unavailable amount remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Map the $128.752 million by legal entity and jurisdiction, document repatriation taxes and transfer restrictions, calculate institution-level regulatory and operating liquidity needs, and rerun the bridge using only demonstrably excess cash.
